Rationale.CS1_Results_vs_Conclusion: All evaluable conclusions in the documentation match the results originally recorded in the code implementation. The plan claims approximately correct results: Capital cities concept lens ~80% (actual 83.4%), family concept lens ~60% (actual 51.6%), present participle token lens ~60% (actual 68.3%), past tense token lens ~65% (actual 85.4%). While there are minor numerical discrepancies (e.g., raw baseline for capital cities claimed ~47% vs actual 39.3%), the core findings that concept lens excels at semantic tasks and token lens excels at grammatical tasks are fully supported by the data. The effective rank claim that performance is maintained at r=256 is also verified (87.2% at rank 256 vs 83.4% at full rank).
Rationale.CS2_Plan_vs_Implementation: All steps in the plan are reflected in the implementation: (1) OV matrix summation implemented in parallelograms.py::get_ov_sum() with k=80 heads; (2) Word embedding extraction at layer ℓ implemented in proj_onto_ov(); (3) Parallelogram arithmetic with nearest neighbor evaluation implemented in get_parallelogram_scores(); (4) All four settings (raw, concept, token, all) compared in all_parallelograms.py; (5) Effective rank analysis with SVD implemented in parallelogram_ranks.py. All planned experiments (Capital Cities, Family Relations, Present Participle, Past Tense, Word2Vec 14 categories, Effective Rank Analysis) have corresponding results in the cache directory.
Rationale.CS3_Effect_Size: The reported effects have clearly non-trivial magnitudes. Absolute improvements range from 32.4 to 53.5 percentage points over raw baselines. Relative improvements range from 112% to 169%. Specific results: Capital cities (concept 83.4% vs raw 39.3%, +44.1pp), Family relations (concept 51.6% vs raw 19.2%, +32.4pp), Present participle (token 68.3% vs raw 30.1%, +38.2pp), Past tense (token 85.4% vs raw 31.9%, +53.5pp). These are large, meaningful effect sizes that far exceed noise and represent practically significant improvements.
Rationale.CS4_Justification: All key design choices are explicitly justified: (1) k=80 heads - justified by reference to prior work on concept/token induction heads; (2) Llama-2-7b model - builds on prior research identifying concept/token heads in this model; (3) Layer selection - systematic sweep across layers with empirical selection of best layer; (4) Task-specific prefixes - documented for word disambiguation; (5) Cosine similarity - standard practice following word2vec tradition. Intermediate conclusions are supported by strong evidence: concept lens superiority for semantic tasks (>2x improvement), token lens superiority for grammatical tasks (>2x improvement), and low-rank sufficiency (performance maintained or improved at r=256).
Rationale.CS5_Statistical_Significance: Key experimental results do NOT report appropriate measures of uncertainty or significance. Missing elements: (1) No error bars in any figures; (2) No confidence intervals reported; (3) No statistical tests (t-tests, ANOVA, etc.) performed; (4) No standard errors or standard deviations computed. While mitigating factors exist (large sample sizes n≈500-1500, very large effect sizes 30-50pp, raw per-sample data stored), the criterion explicitly requires reporting uncertainty measures with clear explanation of variability captured. This was not done despite having the data to compute such measures.
